messages.subject: Problem wit LAVAN and Formative latent variable in comparison with MPLUS and SEM package
parts:
Hi,

I compared MPLUS, LAVAAN and the R package « SEM » for a structural model with a exogenous formative measurement model.

Eta1: formative latent with four endogenous indicators X1,... X4

Eta2 : reflective endogenous latent with for manifests Y1,... Y4

Eta3 : reflective endogenous latent with for manifests Y5,... Y8

Eta1-> Eta2; Eta1->Eta3

I generated data with a link from X1 to Eta2 (Eta 1 do not mediate the link between X1 and Eta 2) to obtain high MI.

I have some problems with LAVAAN.

 1/ MPLUS, LAVAAN and SEM give same estimations, same chisquare, same standardized solutions,…

 2/ MPLUS and SEM give Rsquare for the formative latent variable, LAVAAN do not:

> inspect(RSLT,"r2")

   Y1    Y2    Y3    Y4    Y5    Y6    Y7    Y8  LAT2  LAT3

0.807 0.814 0.809 0.804 0.809 0.812 0.810 0.812 0.362 0.359

 No result for Eta 1

 3/ MPLUS and SEM give the matrix of covariance of latent variables, LAVAAN do not:

> inspect(RSLT,"cov.lv")

Error in `rownames<-`(`*tmp*`, value = c("LAT2", "LAT3")) :

  length of 'dimnames' [1] not equal to array extent

 4/ MPLUS and SEM give very closed Modification Indexes, LAVAAN give very different MI.In different samples, I can obtain MI with LAVAAN which do not permit to see the hidden link between X1 and Eta2. In ecah cases, MPlus and SEM give MI which permit to see the misspecification of the model.


Code MPLUS

x1 with x2-x4;

x2 with x3-x4;

x3 with x4;

eta1 on x1@1 x2-x4;

eta2 by y1@1 y2-y4;

eta3 by y5@1 y6-y8;

eta1 by eta2* eta3 ;

 

Code LAVAAN

MODELE1='

LAT1<~1*X1+X2+X3+X4

LAT2=~1*Y1+Y2+Y3+Y4

LAT3=~1*Y5+Y6+Y7+Y8

X1~~X2

X1~~X3

X1~~X4

X2~~X3

X2~~X4

X3~~X4

LAT2~LAT1

LAT3~LAT1

LAT2~~0*LAT3

LAT1~~LAT1

'

 

Code SEM

model1 <- specifyModel()

X1->L1,lamX1,NA

X2->L1,lamX2,NA

X3->L1,lamX3,NA

X4->L1,lamX4,NA

L2->Y1,lamy1,NA

L2->Y2,lamy2,NA

L2->Y3,lamy3,NA

L2->Y4,lamy4,NA

L3->Y5,lamy5,NA

L3->Y6,lamy6,NA

L3->Y7,lamy7,NA

L3->Y8,lamy8,NA

X1<->X1,ERX1,NA

X2<->X2,ERX2,NA

X3<->X3,ERX3,NA

X4<->X4,ERX4,NA

X1<->X2,covX1X2,NA

X1<->X3,covX1X3,NA

X1<->X4,covX1X4,NA

X2<->X3,covX2X3,NA

X2<->X4,covX2X4,NA

X3<->X4,covX3X4,NA

Y1<-> Y1,ERY1,NA

Y2<-> Y2,ERY2,NA

Y3<-> Y3,ERY3,NA

Y4<-> Y4,ERY4,NA

Y5<-> Y5,ERY5,NA

L2<->L2,NA,1

L3<->L3,NA,1

L1->L2,C2,NA

L1->L3,C3,NA

messages.subject: RE: Problem wit LAVAN and Formative latent variable in comparison with MPLUS and SEM package
parts:
That <~ operator seems to be troublesome.  If you translate your Mplus syntax to lavaan syntax more directly, you might get more similar results.  Instead of :

 

LAT1<~1*X1+X2+X3+X4

How about:

 

LAT1 ~ 1*X1+X2+X3+X4

 

if you want the X1 coefficient fixed to 1.

 

--Ed Rigdon

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Problem wit LAVAN and Formative latent variable in comparison with MPLUS and SEM package
parts:
On 04/03/2015 02:42 PM, Hervé DE BREST wrote:
> 2/ MPLUS and SEM *give Rsquare for the formative latent variable*,
> LAVAAN do not:

That is by design. The '<~' operator is only supposed to be used for
'formative' latent variables in the strict sense, implying: "no residual
error".

If you want to allow for a residual error for your 'LAT1' latent
variable, you need to replace the '<~' formula by this:

LAT1 =~ 0
LAT1 ~ 1*X1+X2+X3+X4

Yves.
